description.narrative: Stakeholders-Farmers: IFC expects the Project to increase access to beet inputs and output markets for smallholder farmers. The Project, through an out-grower scheme, is expected to provide beet seeds, credit and transportation services to 25,000 farmers while also training farmers to adopt climate smart production and post-harvest management practices, which is also expected to standardize quality and consistency of supplies while minimizing losses. Environmental effects: The Project is expected to make a significant contribution to addressing acute climate challenges through solutions that are on a low-carbon and climate-resilient pathway leading to reduction of GHG emissions. The total climate finance portion of the Project is estimated at 54.0%, with 53.1% contributing to climate adaptation and 0.9% contributing to climate mitigation. Economy wide effects: The Project is expected to increase domestic value addition and create jobs along the supply chains through up- and down-stream linkages with related sectors. Competitiveness: The investment will generate market-deepening effects by increasing beet sugar processing, while introducing innovations that significantly improve production and processing performance and efficiencies and maintain the requisite food safety requirements. The scalability of the vertical integration model and adoption of high yielding beet varieties is expected to promote wider adoption across the sector, fostering a growing ecosystem that supports development and integration of farmers in beet supply chains while catalyzing adoption of sustainable practices.

The proposed investment is an up to $40m senior loan, with $20m being for IFCs own account and $20m mobilized, to Nile Agriculture Company S.A.E. (NAC), to be guaranteed by Nile Sugar Company S.A.E. (NS or the Company, and together with NAC, the Obligors or NSG. NS, founded by the Sawiris family (the Sponsors) in 2006, is a leading Egyptian beet sugar refinery producing white sugar and its by-products, including molasses and beet pulp. IFCs loan will be used to finance the development of 13,711 feddans (5,760 hectares) land in Minya, Egypt to cultivate sugar beet and improve its supply chain sustainability, together with required relating infrastructure, machinery and equipment, and working capital (the Project). The Project will directly and indirectly help address increased sugar consumption in Egypt through local production vs. imports.
